question: A cartoon starts at 4 o'clock and lasts 1 hour. At what time does it end?
solution: One hour after 4 o'clock it is 5 o'clock.

A.text: 1 is how long the cartoon lasts, not a time.

C.text: The cartoon ends after it starts, so the time is later, not earlier.

D.text: 4 o'clock is when the cartoon starts.

E.text: 1 hour after 4 o'clock is 5 o'clock, not 6.

question: Lunch is at 12 o'clock. Tom's walk starts 2 hours before lunch. At what time does the walk start?
solution: 11 o'clock is one hour before 12 o'clock, and 10 o'clock is two hours before it.

A.text: 9 o'clock is 3 hours before lunch.

B.text: 11 o'clock is only 1 hour before lunch.

D.text: 12 o'clock is lunch time.

E.text: 2 o'clock is 2 hours after lunch. The walk is before lunch.

question: A film starts at 3 o'clock and ends at 5 o'clock. How many hours long is the film?
solution: From 3 o'clock to 4 o'clock is 1 hour, and from 4 o'clock to 5 o'clock is 1 more hour. That is 2 hours.

A.text: From 3 to 5 o'clock is 2 hours: 3 to 4 and 4 to 5.

B.text: 3 o'clock is when the film starts.

C.text: 5 o'clock is when the film ends.

E.text: You added 3 and 5. Count the hours from 3 to 5.

question: It is 7 o'clock. What time will it be in half an hour?
solution: Half an hour is 30 minutes. 30 minutes after 7:00 it is 7:30.

A.text: In half an hour means later, not earlier.

B.text: 15 minutes is a quarter of an hour. Half an hour is 30 minutes.

C.text: An hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so half an hour is 30 minutes.

D.text: 8:00 is a whole hour later. Half an hour is 30 minutes.

question: A lesson starts at 10:00 and lasts 45 minutes. At what time does it end?
solution: 45 minutes after 10:00 it is 10:45.

B.text: The lesson ends after it starts, not before.

C.text: 10:00 is when the lesson starts.

D.text: You added 15 minutes, not 45.

E.text: The lesson lasts 45 minutes, not 1 hour and 45 minutes.

question: A bus leaves at 9:30 and arrives at 10:00. How many minutes does the trip take?
solution: From 9:30 to 10:00 is half an hour, which is 30 minutes.

A.text: 10 is the hour when the bus arrives.

B.text: From 9:30 to 10:00 is half an hour, not a whole hour.

D.text: You took 30 from 100, but an hour has 60 minutes.

E.text: An hour has 60 minutes, not 100, and the trip is only half an hour.

question: Tim went to bed at 9 o'clock in the evening and got up at 7 o'clock in the morning. How many hours did he sleep?
solution: From 9 in the evening to 12 at midnight is 3 hours. From midnight to 7 in the morning is 7 hours. 3 + 7 = 10 hours.

A.text: You took 7 from 9. Count the hours through midnight.

B.text: 3 hours take you only to midnight. Then there are 7 more hours.

C.text: 12 hours would be from 9 in the evening to 9 in the morning.

E.text: You added 9 and 7. Count the hours from 9 in the evening.

question: The clock shows 5:45. What time will it be in 15 minutes?
solution: 45 minutes and 15 more minutes make 60 minutes, which is a whole hour. So it will be 6:00.

A.text: In 15 minutes means later, not earlier.

B.text: After 59 minutes a new hour begins, so 5:60 is really 6:00.

C.text: You added 30 minutes, not 15.

D.text: You added 1 hour, not 15 minutes.

question: A clock strikes once at 1 o'clock, twice at 2 o'clock, 3 times at 3 o'clock, and so on. How many times does it strike at 1, 2, 3 and 4 o'clock altogether?

B.text: 4 is the last hour, not the number of strikes.

C.text: You added only the strikes at 3 and 4 o'clock.

D.text: You forgot the 1 strike at 1 o'clock.

E.text: You multiplied 3 by 4. Add 1 + 2 + 3 + 4.

question: Anna's watch is 10 minutes fast. It shows 8:20. What is the real time?
solution: A fast watch shows a later time than the real one. The real time is 10 minutes earlier: 8:10.

A.text: You took away 20 minutes, not 10.

C.text: 8:20 is what the watch shows, not the real time.

D.text: A fast watch is ahead, so the real time is earlier, not later.

E.text: The watch is 10 minutes fast, not 1 hour, and the real time is earlier.

question: A cartoon lasts 25 minutes and ends at 5:10. At what time did it start?
solution: From 5:10 go back 10 minutes to 5:00, then 15 more minutes to 4:45. 10 + 15 = 25 minutes.

A.text: 4:15 is 55 minutes before 5:10.

B.text: 4:55 is only 15 minutes before 5:10.

C.text: An hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so there is no 4:85.

E.text: The cartoon started before it ended, so go back, not forward.

question: Lessons start at 8:30. There are 3 lessons of 40 minutes, with a 10-minute break between every two lessons. At what time does the third lesson end?
solution: Three lessons take 3 × 40 = 120 minutes, and there are 2 breaks between them: 20 minutes. In all 140 minutes, which is 2 hours 20 minutes. 8:30 + 2 hours 20 minutes = 10:50.

A.text: An hour has 60 minutes, so there is no 9:70.

B.text: 10:00 is when the second lesson ends.

C.text: You forgot the breaks between the lessons.

D.text: There are only 2 breaks between 3 lessons, not 3.

question: Now it is 11:40. What time was it 50 minutes ago?
solution: Going back 40 minutes from 11:40 gives 11:00. Going back 10 more minutes gives 10:50.

B.text: 10:10 is 90 minutes before 11:40.

C.text: An hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so there is no 10:90.

D.text: You went back only 30 minutes.

E.text: 50 minutes ago means earlier, not later.

question: It takes 3 minutes to boil an egg. How many minutes does it take to boil 3 eggs together in one pot?
solution: All three eggs boil at the same time, so it still takes 3 minutes.

A.text: You divided 3 by 3. More eggs do not boil faster.

C.text: You added 3 and 3. The eggs boil at the same time.

D.text: The eggs boil together in one pot, not one after another.

E.text: The eggs boil together, so the time does not grow.

question: Kolya walks to school in 20 minutes. He must arrive by 8:15. What is the latest time he can leave home?
solution: Go back 15 minutes from 8:15 to 8:00, then 5 more minutes to 7:55. 15 + 5 = 20 minutes.

A.text: 7:45 is 30 minutes before 8:15.

B.text: An hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so there is no 7:95.

D.text: 8:05 is only 10 minutes before 8:15.

E.text: He must leave before the time he arrives, not after.

question: Kate's watch is 5 minutes slow, and Tom's watch is 5 minutes fast. Tom's watch shows 3:10. What does Kate's watch show?
solution: Tom's watch is 5 minutes ahead, so the real time is 3:05. Kate's watch is 5 minutes behind the real time: 3:00.

A.text: 3:05 is the real time. Kate's watch is 5 minutes behind it.

B.text: 3:10 is what Tom's watch shows.

C.text: A slow watch is behind, so Kate's watch shows less than the real time.

D.text: Tom's watch is ahead and Kate's is behind, so Kate's shows 10 minutes less than Tom's, not more.

question: A film starts at 6:40 and lasts 1 hour 30 minutes. At what time does it end?
solution: 1 hour after 6:40 it is 7:40. 30 minutes later it is 8:10.

B.text: The film ends after it starts, so count forward.

C.text: You added only the 30 minutes. Add the hour too.

D.text: An hour has 60 minutes, so 7:70 is really 8:10.

E.text: You added 2 hours, not 1 hour 30 minutes.

question: A clock strikes once at 1 o'clock, twice at 2 o'clock, and so on up to 12 times at 12 o'clock. How many times does it strike at 9, 10, 11 and 12 o'clock altogether?

A.text: 4 is how many hours strike, not how many strikes.

C.text: You added only 9 and 12. Add 10 and 11 too.

D.text: You forgot the 9 strikes at 9 o'clock.

E.text: You multiplied 9 by 12. Add the four numbers.

question: Masha started her homework at 4:50 and finished at 6:10. How long did it take?
solution: From 4:50 to 5:00 is 10 minutes. From 5:00 to 6:10 is 1 hour 10 minutes. In all 1 hour 20 minutes.

A.text: You took 10 from 50. Count from 4:50 to 6:10.

B.text: From 5:00 to 6:10 is 1 hour 10 minutes, but she started 10 minutes before 5:00.

D.text: An hour has 60 minutes, so 6:10 minus 4:50 is not 1 hour 60 minutes.

E.text: From 4 to 6 would be 2 hours only if she had started at 4:00.

question: A train leaves at 11:45. The trip takes 35 minutes. At what time does the train arrive?
solution: 15 minutes after 11:45 it is 12:00. The other 20 minutes take it to 12:20. 15 + 20 = 35.

A.text: The train arrives after it leaves, so count forward.

B.text: An hour has 60 minutes, so 11:80 is really 12:20.

C.text: 12:10 is only 25 minutes after 11:45.

E.text: The 35 minutes are added to 11:45, not to 12:00.

question: Grandma's clock strikes once at every half hour. At every full hour it strikes as many times as the hour: once at 1 o'clock, twice at 2 o'clock, and so on. How many times does it strike from 1:15 to 3:15?
solution: It strikes once at 1:30, twice at 2:00, once at 2:30 and 3 times at 3:00. 1 + 2 + 1 + 3 = 7.

B.text: 4 is how many times the clock rings out, not how many strikes there are.

C.text: You forgot the half-hour strikes at 1:30 and 2:30.

D.text: You missed one of the half-hour strikes.

E.text: 1 o'clock is before 1:15, so it does not count.

question: A merry-go-round ride lasts 5 minutes, and there is a 2-minute break before every next ride. The first ride starts at 3:00. At what time does the fourth ride end?
solution: Four rides take 4 × 5 = 20 minutes, and there are 3 breaks between them: 6 minutes. 3:00 + 26 minutes = 3:26.

A.text: 3:05 is when the first ride ends.

C.text: You forgot the breaks between rides.

D.text: 3:21 is when the fourth ride starts, not when it ends.

E.text: There are 3 breaks between 4 rides, not 4.

question: Tom's clock goes 2 minutes too fast every hour. He sets it right at 8:00 in the morning. What does it show when the real time is 12:00 noon?
solution: From 8:00 to 12:00 there are 4 hours. Each hour the clock gets 2 minutes ahead, so it is 8 minutes ahead: 12:08.

A.text: A fast clock is ahead, so it shows more than 12:00.

B.text: 2 minutes is for one hour. There are 4 hours.

D.text: From 8:00 to 12:00 there are 4 hours, not 5.

E.text: You multiplied 2 by 12. Count only the hours since 8:00.

question: A film started at 5:35 and ended at 7:15. How many minutes long was it?
solution: From 5:35 to 6:35 is 60 minutes, and from 6:35 to 7:15 is 40 more. 60 + 40 = 100 minutes.

A.text: From 5:35 to 6:35 is only 60 minutes; the film went on until 7:15.

B.text: 7 - 5 = 2 hours, but the minutes matter too.

C.text: It is 2 hours minus 20 minutes, not 2 hours plus 20 minutes.

E.text: An hour has 60 minutes, so you cannot just take 535 from 715.

question: Mum puts a cake in the oven at 4:50. It must bake for 1 hour 25 minutes. At what time should she take it out?
solution: 1 hour after 4:50 it is 5:50. 10 more minutes give 6:00, and 15 more give 6:15. 10 + 15 = 25 minutes.

A.text: The cake comes out after it goes in, so count forward.

B.text: You added only the 25 minutes. Add the hour too.

C.text: An hour has 60 minutes, so 5:75 is really 6:15.

D.text: You added 1 hour 35 minutes, not 1 hour 25 minutes.

question: A lesson starts at 10:55 and lasts 45 minutes. At what time does it end?
solution: 5 minutes after 10:55 it is 11:00. The other 40 minutes take it to 11:40.

A.text: The lesson ends after it starts, so count forward.

B.text: An hour has 60 minutes, so 10:100 is not a time.

C.text: 11:00 is only 5 minutes after the start.

E.text: 11:45 is 50 minutes after 10:55.

question: A train leaves at 13:20 and arrives at 15:05 on the same day. How long is the trip?
solution: From 13:20 to 15:20 would be 2 hours. The train arrives 15 minutes earlier, so the trip is 1 hour 45 minutes.

A.text: 1 hour 15 minutes after 13:20 is only 14:35.

B.text: An hour has 60 minutes, so you cannot just take 1320 from 1505.

C.text: You took 5 from 20 instead of counting on from 13:20.

D.text: 2 hours 45 minutes after 13:20 is 16:05.

question: How many minutes are there in two and a half hours?
solution: Two hours are 120 minutes and half an hour is 30 minutes. 120 + 30 = 150.

B.text: 120 minutes are only the 2 hours. Add the half hour.

C.text: Half an hour is 30 minutes, not 10.

D.text: 180 minutes is 3 hours, not two and a half.

E.text: An hour has 60 minutes, not 100.

question: Masha went to sleep at 21:30 and woke up at 7:00 the next morning. How long did she sleep?
solution: From 21:30 to midnight is 2 hours 30 minutes. From midnight to 7:00 is 7 hours. In all 9 hours 30 minutes.

A.text: From 21:30 to midnight is 2 hours 30 minutes, not 1 hour 30 minutes.

C.text: You dropped the half hour: she went to sleep at 21:30.

D.text: From midnight to 7:00 is 7 hours, not 8.

E.text: You took 7 from 21. Count forward through midnight.

question: A clock strikes once at 1 o'clock, twice at 2 o'clock, and so on up to 12 times at 12 o'clock. How many times does it strike from 1 o'clock to 12 o'clock, including both?
solution: 1 + 2 + ... + 12 = 78. Pair the numbers: 1 + 12, 2 + 11 and so on give six pairs of 13, and 6 × 13 = 78.

A.text: 12 is how many hours strike, not how many strikes.

B.text: You forgot the 12 strikes at 12 o'clock.

D.text: You forgot the 1 strike at 1 o'clock.

E.text: You multiplied 12 by 12. Add 1 + 2 + ... + 12.

question: A watch loses 3 minutes every hour. It was set right at 9:00. What does it show when the real time is 13:00?
solution: From 9:00 to 13:00 there are 4 hours. The watch loses 3 minutes each hour: 12 minutes. It shows 13:00 minus 12 minutes = 12:48.

A.text: From 9:00 to 13:00 there are 4 hours, not 5.

B.text: 3 minutes is the loss for one hour. There are 4 hours.

C.text: A watch that loses time is behind, so it shows less than 13:00.

D.text: Losing time means the watch is behind, not ahead.

question: A bus leaves every 12 minutes. The first bus leaves at 6:00. At what time does the sixth bus leave?
solution: Between the first and the sixth bus there are 5 gaps of 12 minutes: 60 minutes. So the sixth bus leaves at 7:00.

B.text: 6:48 is when the fifth bus leaves.

C.text: 60 minutes make a whole hour, so 6:60 is really 7:00.

D.text: Six buses have 5 gaps between them, not 6.

E.text: 7:24 is when the eighth bus leaves.

question: The clock shows 8:40. What time was it 2 hours 55 minutes ago?
solution: 2 hours ago it was 6:40. 40 more minutes back gives 6:00, and 15 more gives 5:45. 40 + 15 = 55 minutes.

A.text: 5:15 is 3 hours 25 minutes before 8:40.

C.text: An hour has 60 minutes, so there is no 5:85.

D.text: 6:45 is only 1 hour 55 minutes before 8:40.

E.text: Ago means earlier, so count back, not forward.

question: School starts at 8:00. Each lesson lasts 45 minutes, and after each lesson there is a 10-minute break. How many lessons end before 12:00?
solution: Lessons end at 8:45, 9:40, 10:35, 11:30 and 12:25. Four of them end before 12:00.

A.text: List the end times: 8:45, 9:40, 10:35 and 11:30. That is four.

B.text: Remember the 10-minute breaks between lessons.

D.text: You divided 4 hours by 40 minutes. List the end times instead.

E.text: 12 is the hour, not the number of lessons.

question: A plane takes off at 22:40 and lands at 1:15 the next day. How long is the flight?
solution: From 22:40 to midnight is 1 hour 20 minutes. From midnight to 1:15 is 1 hour 15 minutes. In all 2 hours 35 minutes.

A.text: From 22:40 to midnight is 1 hour 20 minutes, not 1 hour 10 minutes.

B.text: An hour has 60 minutes, so 75 minutes is really 1 hour 15 minutes.

C.text: From 22:40 to midnight is 1 hour 20 minutes, not 2 hours 20 minutes.

E.text: You took 1:15 away from 22:40. Count forward through midnight.

question: A clock strikes once at every half hour. At every full hour it strikes as many times as the hour, from 1 to 12. How many times does it strike in 12 hours?
solution: The full hours give 1 + 2 + ... + 12 = 78 strikes. There are 12 half hours with 1 strike each. 78 + 12 = 90.

B.text: You forgot the half-hour strikes.

C.text: There are 12 half-hour strikes in 12 hours, not 6.

D.text: In 12 hours there are 12 half hours, not 13.

E.text: You doubled 78. The half hours strike only once each.

question: One clock is 7 minutes fast, and another is 5 minutes slow. The fast clock shows 10:02. What does the slow clock show?
solution: The real time is 7 minutes earlier than the fast clock: 9:55. The slow clock is 5 minutes behind the real time: 9:50.

A.text: 9:55 is the real time. The slow clock is 5 more minutes behind.

C.text: You took away only 5 minutes from the fast clock.

D.text: You took away the difference, 2 minutes. The clocks differ by 7 + 5 = 12 minutes.

E.text: The slow clock shows less than the fast one, not more.

question: A film is 1 hour 50 minutes long. It must end by 21:30. What is the latest time it can start?
solution: Going back 1 hour from 21:30 gives 20:30. Going back 50 more minutes: 30 minutes to 20:00 and 20 more to 19:40.

A.text: 19:20 is 2 hours 10 minutes before 21:30.

B.text: An hour has 60 minutes, so there is no 19:80.

D.text: You went back only 50 minutes. Go back the hour too.

E.text: The film starts before it ends, so count back.

question: A candle burns for 50 minutes. Katya lights 3 candles one after another: she lights the next candle as soon as the previous one goes out. She lights the first candle at 18:40. At what time does the last candle go out?
solution: Three candles burn for 3 × 50 = 150 minutes, which is 2 hours 30 minutes. 18:40 + 2 hours 30 minutes = 21:10.

A.text: 19:30 is when the first candle goes out.

B.text: 20:20 is when the second candle goes out.

C.text: An hour has 60 minutes, so there is no 20:90.

E.text: You added 3 hours, not 2 hours 30 minutes.

question: From 9:15 to 11:45 a school has 3 lessons of the same length, with a 15-minute break between every two lessons. How many minutes long is one lesson?
solution: From 9:15 to 11:45 is 150 minutes. There are 2 breaks: 30 minutes. 150 - 30 = 120 minutes for 3 lessons, so one lesson is 40 minutes.

A.text: 30 minutes is the time of both breaks, not of a lesson.

B.text: There are 2 breaks between 3 lessons, not 3.

C.text: You took away only one break.

D.text: You forgot the breaks.

question: A clock gains 3 minutes every hour. It was set right at 8:00. Now the clock shows 12:12. What is the real time?
solution: In each real hour the clock moves on 63 minutes. It has moved from 8:00 to 12:12, which is 252 minutes = 4 × 63. So 4 real hours have passed: it is 12:00.

A.text: You took away 24 minutes, but the clock is only 12 minutes ahead.

C.text: The clock gains 3 minutes each hour for 4 hours: 12 minutes, not 3.

D.text: 12:12 is what the fast clock shows.

E.text: A fast clock is ahead, so the real time is earlier.

question: Trains leave a station every 25 minutes, starting at 6:10. How many trains leave from 7:00 to 9:00, counting a train that leaves exactly at 7:00?

A.text: The train at 7:00 counts too.

B.text: The next train after 8:40 leaves at 9:05, which is after 9:00.

D.text: 7 trains leave before 9:00 in all, but the two before 7:00 do not count.

E.text: 25 is the number of minutes between trains.

question: It is 14:25 now. What time will it be in 100 minutes?
solution: 100 minutes is 1 hour 40 minutes. 14:25 + 1 hour = 15:25. 35 more minutes give 16:00, and 5 more give 16:05.

A.text: 15:05 is only 40 minutes after 14:25.

B.text: 100 minutes is not 1 hour: an hour has 60 minutes.

C.text: An hour has 60 minutes, so there is no 15:65.

E.text: You added 2 hours, not 1 hour 40 minutes.

question: Petya's watch is 10 minutes slow, but he thinks it is 10 minutes fast. He wants to arrive at school at 9:00, and the walk takes 20 minutes. He leaves home when he believes the real time is 8:40. How many minutes late does he arrive?
solution: He thinks the real time is 10 minutes less than his watch, so he leaves when the watch shows 8:50. But the watch is 10 minutes slow, so the real time is then 9:00. He arrives at 9:20: 20 minutes late.

A.text: Petya is wrong about his watch, so he does not arrive on time.

B.text: There are two 10-minute mistakes, not one.

C.text: The walk itself is not lateness; only the two 10-minute mistakes count.

D.text: Each mistake is 10 minutes; together they make 20, not 40.

question: A digital clock shows hours and minutes from 00:00 to 23:59. How many times in one day does it show four equal digits, like 11:11?
solution: The times are 00:00, 11:11 and 22:22. There is no 33:33, because hours go only up to 23. So there are 3 times.

B.text: 00:00 counts too.

C.text: There is no 33:33: hours go only up to 23.

D.text: Hours go only up to 23 and minutes up to 59; only 00:00, 11:11 and 22:22 work.

E.text: 24 is the number of hours in a day.

question: A wall clock with 12 hours on its face goes 6 minutes too fast every day. At noon today it shows the right time. After how many days will it next show the right time?
solution: The clock shows the right time again when it is exactly 12 hours ahead. 12 hours = 720 minutes. 720 ÷ 6 = 120 days.

A.text: After 10 days the clock is only 1 hour ahead.

B.text: 12 is the number of hours on the face.

D.text: 12 hours are 720 minutes, not 360.

E.text: The face has 12 hours, so being 12 hours ahead is enough; 24 hours is not needed.

question: A clock strikes once at a quarter past, at half past and at a quarter to every hour. At every full hour it strikes as many times as the hour, from 1 to 12. How many times does it strike in a whole day of 24 hours?
solution: In 12 hours the full hours give 1 + 2 + ... + 12 = 78 strikes, so 156 in a day. Every hour has 3 quarter strikes: 3 × 24 = 72. 156 + 72 = 228.

A.text: The full hours strike twice a day: 78 + 78 = 156, not 78.

B.text: You forgot the quarter strikes.

C.text: There are 3 quarter strikes each hour, not 2.

E.text: At the full hour the clock strikes the hour, not an extra quarter: 3 quarter strikes per hour, not 4.

question: The train Swift leaves at 7:50 and arrives at 10:35. The train Pony takes 25 minutes longer for its trip and leaves at 8:20. At what time does Pony arrive?
solution: Swift's trip from 7:50 to 10:35 takes 2 hours 45 minutes. Pony's trip is 25 minutes longer: 3 hours 10 minutes. 8:20 + 3 hours 10 minutes = 11:30.

A.text: Pony also leaves 30 minutes later than Swift, so add those 30 minutes too.

B.text: Pony's trip is 25 minutes longer than Swift's.

C.text: 11:55 is 3 hours 35 minutes after 8:20.

D.text: You added one hour too many.

question: A digital clock shows hours and minutes from 00:00 to 23:59. How many times in a day does it show the same number for the hours and for the minutes, like 05:05 or 12:12?
solution: The hours go from 00 to 23, and each hour has one matching minute: 00:00, 01:01, ..., 23:23. That is 24 times.

B.text: The clock shows 24 hours, not 12.

C.text: 00:00 counts too.

D.text: 60 is the number of minutes in an hour.

E.text: 1440 is the number of minutes in a whole day.

question: Sasha's watch was 2 minutes slow at 8:00 on Monday. Every day it loses 3 more minutes. What does it show when the real time is 8:00 on Friday of the same week?
solution: From Monday 8:00 to Friday 8:00 there are 4 days. The watch loses 4 × 3 = 12 more minutes, so it is 2 + 12 = 14 minutes slow: 7:46.

A.text: From Monday to Friday there are 4 days, not 5.

C.text: The watch was already 2 minutes slow on Monday.

D.text: From Monday to Friday there are 4 days, not 3.

E.text: A slow watch is behind, so it shows less than 8:00.
